destination.title: Flux compactifications, orientifolds and quantum flux consistency
destination.question: How do fluxes, projections, localized sources and dualities constrain compactification geometry, effective dynamics and quantum sectors?
destination.summary: A proposed navigation family with a compactification core and adjacent quantum and brane questions. Numerical membership and source-selection labels are not scientific acceptance criteria: the source-inclusive Bianchi analysis and ten-dimensional backreaction probe belong in the core, while generalized complex geometry supplies a method bridge.

systems: Type II compactifications and orientifolds, including massive IIA
M/F-theory, Type I and heterotic comparisons where explicitly supplied
Adjacent self-dual gauge fields, S-fold probe theories and two-dimensional type-0 strings
targets: Flux consistency, quantization and source cancellation
Effective actions, spectra, potentials, vacua and stability
Orientifold projections, brane sectors and quantum consistency
regimes: Four-dimensional reductions dominate; six- and seven-dimensional questions remain separate
Classical, perturbative, nonperturbative and quantum free-field analyses are alternatives
Toroidal, Calabi–Yau, generalized-structure and nongeometric settings are source-specific
assumptions: Shared navigation does not imply shared field content, supersymmetry, source treatment or quantization prescription
Effective-theory consistency and higher-dimensional realization require separate assessment
conventions: Retain source dates and distinctions between announced targets, reported examples and unresolved extensions
Graph relations describe exact source objects; they do not automatically impose premises on retrieval questions
includes: Construction questions, methodological questions and necessary-condition tests
Alternate homes for sources outside the compactification core
excludes: A universal classification of string vacua
Automatic equivalence of questions sharing flux or orientifold terminology
Universal control, localization or uplift claims inferred from effective potentials

sources.title: Toroidal orientifolds in IIA with general NS-NS fluxes

evidence.text: Which generalized NS-NS flux configurations admit consistent four-dimensional IIA orientifold descriptions and useful moduli potentials?

sources.title: Toroidal orientifolds in IIA with general NS-NS fluxes

evidence.text: Which combinations of H, metric, Q, and R flux admit consistent four-dimensional N=1 IIA orientifold descriptions, how do they generate D-terms and stabilize moduli, and which admit ten-dimensional constructions with correct flux quantization?

sources.title: Toroidal orientifolds in IIA with general NS-NS fluxes

evidence.text: Which effective generalized-flux configurations have ten-dimensional origins, and can all their constraints be formulated using orientifold cohomology?

sources.title: AdS4 flux vacua in type II superstrings and their domain-wall solutions

evidence.text: How does retained field content affect perturbative IIA stabilization with RR zero- and four-form fluxes and NS three-form flux, without metric flux?

sources.title: Lectures on Nongeometric Flux Compactifications

evidence.text: Which nongeometric flux effective theories possess complete string descriptions, and how far do toroidal constructions extend? The outstanding questions concern R-flux, worldsheet consistency, non-toroidal compactifications and the relation to generalized-structure reductions.

sources.title: Gaugings at angles from orientifold reductions

evidence.text: What higher-dimensional orientifold mechanism produces relative electromagnetic SL(2) angles between gauge factors in four-dimensional N=4 supergravity, and how do bulk fluxes and local source terms cooperate in moduli stabilization?

sources.title: Flux moduli stabilisation, Supergravity algebras and no-go theorems

evidence.text: Which flux-induced supergravity algebras are compatible with the isotropic T⁶/(Z₂×Z₂) orientifolds, and which resulting effective models can evade necessary no-go conditions for nonsupersymmetric Minkowski or de Sitter vacua with stabilized moduli?

sources.title: Exceptional Flux Compactifications

evidence.text: How can source-free type II flux backgrounds be embedded into maximal four-dimensional gauged supergravity so that their critical points, full scalar spectra, supersymmetry and gauge groups can be determined?

sources.title: Gauged supergravities and non-geometric Q/R-fluxes from asymmetric orbifold CFT`s

evidence.text: How can exact freely acting orbifold CFTs determine the flux algebra of effective gauged supergravity and realize Q/R backgrounds, including simultaneous fluxes and examples without geometric T-duals?

sources.title: NS-branes, source corrected Bianchi identities, and more on backgrounds with non-geometric fluxes

evidence.text: How do NS-branes source ten-dimensional NSNS Bianchi identities, and when can β-supergravity describe backgrounds with non-geometric fluxes geometrically? The second question includes whether the identified backgrounds yield physics beyond geometric T-duality orbits.

sources.title: KK-monopoles and G-structures in M-theory/type IIA reductions

evidence.text: Can metric fluxes and moduli in M-theory/massive IIA STU models be represented by intrinsic torsion, permitting higher-dimensional uplifts even when the Jacobi constraints required for ordinary twisted-torus reductions are relaxed?

sources.title: Geometric non-geometry

evidence.text: Which STU models containing fluxes classified as non-geometric in a toroidal description can instead arise from geometric M-theory reductions on spaces with different topologies?

sources.title: Type IIB on $S^{3}\times S^{3}$ through $Q$ & $P$ fluxes

evidence.text: Can particular STU superpotentials interpreted as non-geometric Q/P flux on a torus instead arise from geometric, non-toroidal type-IIB backgrounds, thereby breaking no-scale behavior without nonperturbative effects?

sources.title: Minkowski 3-forms, Flux String Vacua, Axion Stability and Naturalness

evidence.text: How do Minkowski three-forms encode internal fluxes, moduli auxiliary fields and axion potentials in Type II orientifolds, and can their gauge and duality symmetries constrain corrections sufficiently to stabilize large-field potentials or interacting scalar masses?

sources.title: Open string multi-branched and Kähler potentials

evidence.text: How do D-brane position and Wilson-line modes enter the flux-generated F-term potential together with closed-string moduli, and what do its discrete symmetries imply for holomorphic coordinates and the Kähler potential?

sources.title: The Type IIA Flux Potential, 4-forms and Freed-Witten anomalies

evidence.text: How can the classical type IIA flux F-term potential, including D6-brane moduli and localised sources, be organised through four-forms, axion polynomials and microscopic anomaly cancellation?

sources.title: Bounds on Slow Roll and the de Sitter Swampland

evidence.text: Does the universal-modulus bounding strategy extend to a seven-dimensional IIA example? The source finds a bound after omitting F2, while retaining F2 defeats the attempted bound. Its physical exclusion is attributed to an orientifold projection.

sources.title: Some remarks on Swampland conjectures, fluxes and K-theory in IIB toroidal compactifications

evidence.text: How do three-form fluxes, nonperturbative superpotential terms, and non-BPS tension compete in the U,S,T sector of an isotropic IIB orientifold?

sources.title: A Landscape of AdS Flux Vacua

evidence.text: Which supersymmetric and nonsupersymmetric classical flux extrema can be organized algebraically in type IIA Calabi–Yau orientifolds, which are perturbatively stable, and how do mobile D6-branes extend them?

sources.title: Rigid nongeometric orientifolds and the swampland

evidence.text: Can nongeometric fluxes support de-Sitter critical points in a rigid type II orientifold after all NS-NS consistency constraints are imposed? The paper tests an explicit toroidal sector with no complex-structure moduli.

sources.title: 6D (1,1) Gauged Supergravities from Orientifold Compactifications

evidence.text: Which orientifold reductions of type II/M-theory yield nonchiral N=(1,1) gauged supergravity in six dimensions, how do their fluxes map to embedding tensors, and which maximally symmetric extrema occur in the resulting restricted flux sectors?

sources.title: Testing Swampland Conjectures with Machine Learning

evidence.text: How do constrained RR, NS-NS and non-geometric integer fluxes determine extrema and scalar spectra in an isotropic Type IIB compactification?

sources.title: Dynamical tadpoles and Weak Gravity Constraints

evidence.text: Which compact flux background admits stabilized D7 positions and a small displacement? The paper uses factorized tori, quotient-dependent quantization, and an explicit pair of RR and NSNS three-forms.

sources.title: Weak gravity bounds in asymptotic string compactifications

evidence.text: How can elementary charge ratios constrain restricted tree-level orientifold flux-potential gradients?

sources.title: Exploring the landscape of (anti-) de Sitter and Minkowski solutions: group manifolds, stability and scale separation

evidence.text: Which internal geometries and scalar stability properties occur in type-II supergravity backgrounds with maximally symmetric four-dimensional spacetime and smeared orientifold/D-brane sources?

sources.title: Taxonomy of scalar potential with <math display="inline"><mi>U</mi></math>-dual fluxes

evidence.text: How can the large four-dimensional scalar potential induced by U-dual-completed type IIB fluxes be reorganized to expose its flux-bilinear structure, constraints and possible higher-dimensional origins?

sources.title: Flux Landscape with enhanced symmetry not on SL(2, ℤ) elliptic points

evidence.text: How do geometric dualities, enhanced symmetries and a bounded flux D3 charge organize physically distinct SUSY Minkowski F-term solutions on two one-complex-structure toroidal orientifolds?

sources.title: Massive IIA flux compactifications with dynamical open strings

evidence.text: How do dynamical D6-brane positions, Wilson lines and non-Abelian gauge data modify massive IIA flux compactifications, their four-dimensional scalar potential, AdS vacua and perturbative reliability?

sources.title: Geometry of orientifolds with NS NS B flux

evidence.text: What geometry explains gauge-rank reduction, mixed-sector multiplicities and T-duality in orientifolds with quantized NS-NS B-flux, and what additional consistency conditions arise for K3 orbifolds?

sources.title: General N=1 supersymmetric fluxes in massive type IIA string theory

evidence.text: Which fluxes and internal geometries of massive type IIA admit four-dimensional N=1 vacua with SU(3) or SU(2) structure, and how might these backgrounds accommodate chiral D-brane gauge sectors and moduli stabilization?

sources.title: Toroidal orientifolds in IIA with general NS-NS fluxes

evidence.text: Transport reference R-R polyforms, differentiate, and match operator coefficients. Restrict outputs to one lower/base index per flux; unrestricted generalized fluxes and R flux are not supplied.

sources.title: AdS4 flux vacua in type II superstrings and their domain-wall solutions

evidence.text: Specify duality directions and transform bulk fields, sources and the effective Kähler/superpotential pair. In these constructions, transverse NS5 duality produces KK monopoles and geometric flux.

sources.title: Lectures on Nongeometric Flux Compactifications

evidence.text: Enumerate admissible flux vectors, solve their consistency conditions, eliminate S and U, and numerically solve for physical τ roots. Record g_s and Λ while keeping root-finding, duality identifications and string-theory validity as separate tasks.

sources.title: Gaugings at angles from orientifold reductions

evidence.text: Use the embedding tensor fαMNP and ξαM and its quadratic consistency constraints. Singlet projection removes ξ and retains four SO(6,6) three-form components; constraints prohibit simultaneous barred and unbarred components within either three-direction block.

sources.title: Flux moduli stabilisation, Supergravity algebras and no-go theorems

evidence.text: Match IIB potential terms to IIA volume–dilaton scaling powers, including localized sources and axion dependence. The proposed subsequent search analytically eliminates S and T before numerical treatment of Z; details of the minimization procedure are deferred.

sources.title: Exceptional Flux Compactifications

evidence.text: Use SU(8) formulas for the scalar equations, all 70 scalar masses and Killing-spinor conditions. At the chosen origin, flux constraints and stationarity become algebraic equations; gauge brackets then identify the gauging.

sources.title: Lectures on Generalized Complex Geometry for Physicists

evidence.text: How does generalized complex geometry express supersymmetry conditions for type II flux compactifications and D-brane embeddings, extending the Calabi–Yau description without fluxes?

sources.title: TASI Lectures on Remnants from the String Landscape

evidence.text: How do branes, orientifolds, intersections, and fluxes generate four-dimensional gauge sectors and chiral matter?

sources.title: Topological mirror symmetry with fluxes

evidence.text: What intrinsic topology carries the integer NS flux under mirror symmetry, and which additional geometric data and nonharmonic forms are needed for effective theories on SU(3)-structure manifolds?

sources.title: Duality symmetric massive type 2 theories in D=8 and D=6

evidence.text: Determine which perturbative T-dualities survive generalized T² and T⁴ reductions of Romans massive IIA with RR fluxes, and use them to relate massive IIA branes to ordinary IIA and eleven-dimensional backgrounds.

sources.title: An Orientifold of type IIB theory on K3

evidence.text: Can an orientifold of Type-IIB on K3 realize six-dimensional N=1 supersymmetry with multiple tensor multiplets, consistent open-string matter, canceled tadpoles, and canceled gravitational and gauge anomalies?

sources.title: Counting fermionic zero modes on M5 with fluxes

evidence.text: How do background fluxes alter M5 fermionic zero modes and the arithmetic-genus restriction on instanton-generated superpotentials?

sources.title: N=1 effective potential from dual type-IIA D6/O6 orientifolds with general fluxes

evidence.text: How do general fluxes and D6/O6 sources determine the four-dimensional N=1 potential directly from ten-dimensional type IIA, and which consistency conditions and supersymmetric moduli-stabilizing vacua extend beyond truncated N=4 gaugings?

sources.title: Magnetized E3-brane instantons in F-theory

evidence.text: How do E3 world-volume fluxes change neutral fermionic zero modes and superpotential selection criteria in F-theory, while consistently incorporating SL(2,Z) monodromies?

sources.title: Open strings in IIB orientifold reductions

evidence.text: How can dynamical open strings, non-Abelian brane gauge groups and internal Yang–Mills flux be incorporated into the dictionary between type IIB orientifold compactifications and six-dimensional N=(1,1) gauged supergravity?

sources.title: Strings on orientifolds

evidence.text: Can Type IIB orientifolds produce six-dimensional N=1 vacua with multiple tensor multiplets and varied gauge groups, and higher-dimensional examples with useful dual descriptions, especially M-theory on a Klein bottle?

sources.title: Swampland conjectures for type IIB orientifolds with closed-string U(1)s

evidence.text: Which moduli and gauge fields survive an O3/O7 orientifold? Complex-structure deformations and closed-string U(1)s occupy different N=1 multiplets after the parent vector sector splits.

sources.title: Metastable vacua from torsion and machine learning

evidence.text: What classical ten-dimensional ingredients generate the proposed four-dimensional vacuum potential? The starting source set contains three-form fluxes, D3-branes and O3− planes, while the torsional five-form and wrapped D5 ingredients are introduced subsequently.

sources.title: D6-branes and torsion

evidence.text: How do integral torsion groups determine the consistent BPS D6-brane spectrum, open-string moduli, discrete configurations, and possible chirality constraints in type IIA flux compactifications?

sources.title: Orientifold Calabi-Yau threefolds with divisor involutions and string landscape

evidence.text: Which nontrivial holomorphic divisor-exchange Z2 involutions yield consistent Type IIB orientifolds with odd (1,1) cohomology, and what fixed O-planes, free actions, parity splittings, and naive tadpole-compatible configurations occur?

sources.title: A landscape of orientifold vacua

evidence.text: Which O3/O7 orientifolds descend from tractable CICY descriptions, what topological data characterize them, and which satisfy necessary topological conditions for ultralight throat axions?

sources.title: Nongeometric flux compactifications

evidence.text: Construct a T-duality-complete flux superpotential and flux constraints for a simple type II toroidal orientifold, including nongeometric Q- and R-fluxes, and clarify which structures admit local or global geometric interpretations.

sources.title: From ten to four and back again: How to generalize the geometry

evidence.text: How is a generalized flux compactification projected to the desired N=1 field content? The orientifold combines a world-sheet operation with an internal involution, with spinorial consistency determining whether a left-moving fermion-parity factor is needed.

sources.title: Superstrings with intrinsic torsion

evidence.text: Which intrinsic-torsion conditions are necessary and sufficient for static NS-NS string backgrounds to preserve supersymmetry, what additional Bianchi conditions produce solutions of the equations of motion, and how can these conditions generate explicit flux geometries?

sources.title: Lectures on Nongeometric Flux Compactifications

evidence.text: How does T-duality enlarge the set of Type II flux compactifications beyond ordinary target-space manifolds? The lectures study backgrounds generated from NS-NS three-form flux, rather than attempting a classification of all nongeometric conformal field theories.

sources.title: Zp charged branes in flux compactifications

evidence.text: How do background fluxes modify the conserved charges and allowed decay processes of wrapped branes giving four-dimensional particles, strings and domain walls, and how are these changes represented by discrete gauge symmetries and identifications of flux vacua?

sources.title: Classification of discrete modular symmetries in Type IIB flux vacua

evidence.text: Which modular subgroups survive three-form fluxes on toroidal orientifolds, and how do flux quantization, tadpole cancellation and magnetized D-branes constrain their realization?

sources.title: D-terms from generalized NS-NS fluxes in type II

evidence.text: How do generalized NS-NS fluxes enter four-dimensional N=1 type-II orientifold theories, and which fluxes charge R-R axions and generate D-term scalar potentials? The motivation is a richer potential for moduli stabilization and possible de Sitter or inflationary applications.

sources.title: The Effective action of N = 1 Calabi-Yau orientifolds

evidence.text: Determine the four-dimensional N=1 bulk effective action of type IIB Calabi–Yau orientifolds with background fluxes, including Kähler potential, superpotential, gauge kinetic functions, and chiral versus linear multiplet descriptions.

sources.title: Fermion Wavefunctions in Magnetized branes: Theta identities and Yukawa couplings

evidence.text: How can globally defined fermion/scalar wavefunctions and Yukawa overlaps be constructed for toroidal magnetized branes with oblique, mutually noncommuting flux matrices, including mixed eigenvalue signatures that exclude the familiar positive-chirality basis?

sources.title: From ten to four and back again: How to generalize the geometry

evidence.text: How can supersymmetric Euclidean D-branes be described using the spinor data of a Minkowskian flux background? The continuation must distinguish independent Euclidean chiralities while preserving the intended supersymmetry-component count.

sources.title: A geometric action for non-geometric fluxes

evidence.text: What geometric interpretation can be assigned to non-geometric Q and R fluxes, and can they enter a higher-dimensional action with manifest diffeomorphism covariance?

sources.title: The web of swampland conjectures and the TCC bound

evidence.text: How should external four-form flux components enter a four-dimensional scalar potential obtained from a type-II compactification?

sources.title: The Effective action of type II Calabi-Yau orientifolds

evidence.text: What geometric data determine the four-dimensional N=1 bulk effective actions of type II Calabi-Yau orientifolds, including flux potentials, chiral coordinates, dual linear multiplets and higher-dimensional embeddings?

sources.title: Rigid nongeometric orientifolds and the swampland

evidence.text: Which fields survive the IIB quotient? The holomorphic sign reversal leaves three even (1,1) directions, three Kähler moduli Tα, no odd moduli Ga, and two odd three-form directions.

sources.title: Romans type IIA theory and the heterotic strings

evidence.text: Can RR flux in a two-torus reduction restore duality covariance of massive type IIA supergravity and provide a route from Romans backgrounds to heterotic backgrounds despite their different massive tensor and vector descriptions?

sources.title: D = 4, N=1, type IIB orientifolds

evidence.text: Which toroidal type IIB orientifolds yield consistent D=4, N=1 vacua, how restrictive are their tadpole conditions, and what do alternative projections imply for spectra, candidate heterotic duals and effective interactions?

sources.title: Rigid nongeometric orientifolds and the swampland

evidence.text: Does harmonic nilpotency constrain this type IIA orientifold? The parity projection removes the even-form flux sector, and rigidity trivializes the remaining antisymmetric relation.

sources.title: Towards Minkowski Vacua in Type II String Compactifications

evidence.text: Can non-geometric type II orientifolds admit supersymmetric Minkowski vacua with every retained modulus stabilized, tadpoles satisfied, and parametrically large fields at weak string coupling?

sources.title: Generalized N=1 orientifold compactifications and the Hitchin functionals

evidence.text: Determine the bulk four-dimensional N=1 spectrum, Kähler potentials and flux/torsion superpotentials of generalized type II orientifolds, and test candidate mirrors of Calabi–Yau orientifolds with restricted electric and magnetic NS–NS flux.

sources.title: The Effective action of type IIA Calabi-Yau orientifolds

evidence.text: What are the bulk chiral coordinates, Kähler potential, gauge kinetic functions and flux superpotential of generic type IIA Calabi–Yau orientifolds, and how do their effective actions connect to special G2 compactifications and orientifold mirror symmetry?

sources.title: Toroidal orientifolds in IIA with general NS-NS fluxes

evidence.text: What is the R-R charge lattice when NS-NS coefficients are logarithms of integral monodromies rather than integer inherited-form coefficients?

sources.title: Non-perturbative and Flux superpotentials for Type I strings on the Z(3) orbifold

evidence.text: Which ED5, ED1 and closed-string flux effects generate superpotentials in the Type I Z3 orientifold with Wilson lines, how does anomalous U(1) invariance constrain them, and could their combination stabilize moduli?

sources.title: Flux-induced SUSY-breaking soft terms on D7-D3 brane systems

evidence.text: Can RR/NSNS three-form fluxes generate calculable SUSY-breaking soft terms and stabilize D7-brane moduli while retaining classical four-dimensional Minkowski backgrounds?

sources.title: On brane gaugino condensates in 10d

evidence.text: Determine how compact geometry changes cancellation of a localized codimension-two source when bulk flux periods are quantized.

sources.title: Rigid nongeometric orientifolds and the swampland

evidence.text: Do the additional toroidal constraints persist on generic rigid Calabi–Yau orientifolds and obstruct simultaneous H,Q flux there?

sources.title: Hitchin functionals in N=2 supergravity

evidence.text: How can type II supergravity on backgrounds admitting eight selected supercharges be organized in an N=2-like form, and how do intrinsic torsion and fluxes determine its geometry, prepotentials and possible four-dimensional truncations?

sources.title: Moduli stabilization in asymptotic flux compactifications

evidence.text: Which fields and cohomology sectors enter the flux-stabilization problem? The paper retains the axio-dilaton and orientifold-odd complex-structure sector of a Type IIB O3/O7 compactification.

sources.title: Mirror symmetry in generalized Calabi-Yau compactifications

evidence.text: What compactification geometry supplies the missing mirror partners of electric NS three-form flux, and can its type IIA low-energy action match type IIB on a Calabi–Yau threefold?

sources.title: Lectures on Nongeometric Flux Compactifications

evidence.text: Which fields survive in a tractable orientifold model used to compare geometric and nongeometric flux potentials? The construction identifies the N=4 spectrum, considers flux breaking to N=1, and then restricts to three identical two-tori.

sources.title: Asymptotic Flux Compactifications and the Swampland

evidence.text: How does primitive internal four-form flux generate a complex-structure potential? The M/F-theory expression combines a moduli-dependent Hodge norm with a topological flux pairing constrained by the curvature tadpole.

sources.title: Beyond Twisted Tori

evidence.text: Which flux and localized-source combinations define consistent compactifications and effective theories when geometrical flux changes the internal topology? The paper studies this question classically, principally for type-IIA orientifolds with four-dimensional supersymmetry.

sources.title: (Non-)commutative closed string on T-dual toroidal backgrounds

evidence.text: Does the Q-flux T-dual of a three-torus with H-flux exhibit closed-string coordinate noncommutativity, supporting the conjecture that the coordinate commutator is proportional to a winding-cycle integral of Q?

sources.title: Lectures on Nongeometric Flux Compactifications

evidence.text: What happens to quantized NS-NS flux under repeated fiber T-duality? The review uses a flat T³ with integer H-flux as a simple local illustration whose monodromies can be computed explicitly.

sources.title: New Examples of Flux Vacua

evidence.text: Which geometric type IIA and massive IIA Minkowski flux backgrounds arise by T-dualizing toroidal type IIB orientifolds, and how do their fluxes, localized-source tadpoles and equations of motion evade the compactification no-go obstruction?

sources.title: Tadpole versus anomaly cancellation in D = 4, D = 6 compact IIB orientifolds

evidence.text: When are RR tadpole cancellation and gauge anomaly cancellation equivalent in compact D=4,6 Type IIB orientifolds, and do tadpole conditions uniquely determine the gauge group?

sources.title: A Note on superconformal N=2 theories and orientifolds

evidence.text: What type IIB orientifolds are T-dual to elliptic type IIA configurations with O6-planes, especially oppositely charged pairs, and how do twisted tadpole conditions encode four-dimensional N=2 finiteness?

sources.title: Beyond Twisted Tori

evidence.text: Do nongeometric fluxes possess source solitons analogous to NS5 and KK5 objects, and can their contributions relax the corresponding flux constraints? The paper poses this as an unresolved extension.

sources.title: On Missing Bianchi Identities in Cohomology Formulation

evidence.text: Which quadratic NS-NS flux constraints are missed by the known cohomology formulation of type IIA Bianchi identities, and can their structure be expressed using topological data for applications beyond toroidal orientifolds?

sources.title: Fixing moduli in exact type IIA flux vacua

evidence.text: Do the supersymmetric type IIA flux vacua obtained from four-dimensional effective theory admit ten-dimensional descriptions, how does flux/O6 backreaction modify Calabi–Yau geometry, and how does ten-dimensional flux quantization fix moduli?

sources.title: Fluxes, moduli fixing and MSSM-like vacua in a simple IIA orientifold

evidence.text: Which moduli can RR, NS and metric fluxes stabilize in a simple IIA orientifold, and can the resulting backgrounds support consistent intersecting-D6 configurations with MSSM-like spectra?

sources.title: Rigid nongeometric orientifolds and the swampland

evidence.text: Which parities define this N=1 IIA model? The visually confirmed antiholomorphic sign reversal leaves three odd (1,1) directions, no even directions, and a three-form pair with A0 even and B^0 odd.

sources.title: $\beta$-supergravity: a ten-dimensional theory with non-geometric fluxes, and its geometric framework

evidence.text: Can a ten-dimensional NSNS reformulation identify non-geometric Q- and R-fluxes, explain their geometric structures, and provide an origin for some four-dimensional gauged supergravities?

sources.title: Supersymmetric SU(5) GUT with stabilized moduli

evidence.text: The compactification provides a concrete setting in which magnetic fluxes determine geometry and open-string intersections produce charged matter. Brane multiplicities, winding maps, integral Chern numbers, and orientifold images supply the discrete construction data.

sources.title: Supersymmetric D-branes and calibrations on general N=1 backgrounds

evidence.text: How can supersymmetric D-branes in general four-dimensional N=1 type II flux backgrounds be characterized geometrically, and how do their supersymmetry conditions encode energy minimization through generalized calibrations?

sources.title: Flux induced SUSY breaking soft terms

evidence.text: Which local type IIB backgrounds induce supersymmetry-breaking soft terms on D3-branes, and how do flux components determine their pattern and four-dimensional interpretation?

sources.title: GUTs in Type IIB Orientifold Compactifications

evidence.text: Can compact Type IIB orientifolds realize SU(5) GUT sectors with massless hypercharge, suitable matter and Yukawa couplings while satisfying global charge cancellation, flux quantization and supersymmetry constraints?

sources.title: Progress in D-brane model building

evidence.text: How can D-branes produce weakly coupled four-dimensional N=1 type II orientifold vacua with semi-realistic gauge sectors, and how do background fluxes change the allowed branes, effective couplings, moduli stabilization and supersymmetry breaking?

sources.title: A Note on the dS Swampland Conjecture, Non‐BPS Branes and K‐Theory

evidence.text: Which fields and wrapped cycles survive the Type IIA orientifold projection? The setting distinguishes parity sectors carrying Kähler moduli, three-form chiral multiplets, R-R vectors, O6-planes, and intersecting D6-branes.

sources.title: Moduli Stabilization in Non-Geometric Backgrounds

evidence.text: Can intrinsically non-geometric type IIB orientifolds without Kähler moduli stabilize the remaining moduli using quantized R-R and NS-NS fluxes alone, satisfy tadpole cancellation, and yield supersymmetric Minkowski or AdS vacua?

destinations.title: Which generalized NS-NS flux configurations admit consistent four-dimensional IIA orientifold descriptions and useful moduli potentials?

Which combinations of H, metric, Q, and R flux admit consistent four-dimensional N=1 IIA orientifold descriptions, how do they generate D-terms and stabilize moduli, and which admit ten-dimensional constructions with correct flux quantization?
Which effective generalized-flux configurations have ten-dimensional origins, and can all their constraints be formulated using orientifold cohomology?
How does retained field content affect perturbative IIA stabilization with RR zero- and four-form fluxes and NS three-form flux, without metric flux?

Which nongeometric flux effective theories possess complete string descriptions, and how far do toroidal constructions extend? The outstanding questions concern R-flux, worldsheet consistency, non-toroidal compactifications and the relation to generalized-structure reductions.

What higher-dimensional orientifold mechanism produces relative electromagnetic SL(2) angles between gauge factors in four-dimensional N=4 supergravity, and how do bulk fluxes and local source terms cooperate in moduli stabilization?

Which flux-induced supergravity algebras are compatible with the isotropic T⁶/(Z₂×Z₂) orientifolds, and which resulting effective models can evade necessary no-go conditions for nonsupersymmetric Minkowski or de Sitter vacua with stabilized moduli?

How can source-free type II flux backgrounds be embedded into maximal four-dimensional gauged supergravity so that their critical points, full scalar spectra, supersymmetry and gauge groups can be determined?

How can exact freely acting orbifold CFTs determine the flux algebra of effective gauged supergravity and realize Q/R backgrounds, including simultaneous fluxes and examples without geometric T-duals?

How do NS-branes source ten-dimensional NSNS Bianchi identities, and when can β-supergravity describe backgrounds with non-geometric fluxes geometrically? The second question includes whether the identified backgrounds yield physics beyond geometric T-duality orbits.

Can metric fluxes and moduli in M-theory/massive IIA STU models be represented by intrinsic torsion, permitting higher-dimensional uplifts even when the Jacobi constraints required for ordinary twisted-torus reductions are relaxed?
Which STU models containing fluxes classified as non-geometric in a toroidal description can instead arise from geometric M-theory reductions on spaces with different topologies?

Can particular STU superpotentials interpreted as non-geometric Q/P flux on a torus instead arise from geometric, non-toroidal type-IIB backgrounds, thereby breaking no-scale behavior without nonperturbative effects?

How do Minkowski three-forms encode internal fluxes, moduli auxiliary fields and axion potentials in Type II orientifolds, and can their gauge and duality symmetries constrain corrections sufficiently to stabilize large-field potentials or interacting scalar masses?
Which discrete-flux variants of four-dimensional N=3-preserving S-folds exist, and how do they determine D3-brane probe theories, central charges, Coulomb operators and discrete symmetries?

How do D-brane position and Wilson-line modes enter the flux-generated F-term potential together with closed-string moduli, and what do its discrete symmetries imply for holomorphic coordinates and the Kähler potential?
How can the classical type IIA flux F-term potential, including D6-brane moduli and localised sources, be organised through four-forms, axion polynomials and microscopic anomaly cancellation?

Does the universal-modulus bounding strategy extend to a seven-dimensional IIA example? The source finds a bound after omitting F2, while retaining F2 defeats the attempted bound. Its physical exclusion is attributed to an orientifold projection.
How do three-form fluxes, nonperturbative superpotential terms, and non-BPS tension compete in the U,S,T sector of an isotropic IIB orientifold?

Which supersymmetric and nonsupersymmetric classical flux extrema can be organized algebraically in type IIA Calabi–Yau orientifolds, which are perturbatively stable, and how do mobile D6-branes extend them?

Can nongeometric fluxes support de-Sitter critical points in a rigid type II orientifold after all NS-NS consistency constraints are imposed? The paper tests an explicit toroidal sector with no complex-structure moduli.

Which orientifold reductions of type II/M-theory yield nonchiral N=(1,1) gauged supergravity in six dimensions, how do their fluxes map to embedding tensors, and which maximally symmetric extrema occur in the resulting restricted flux sectors?
How do constrained RR, NS-NS and non-geometric integer fluxes determine extrema and scalar spectra in an isotropic Type IIB compactification?

Which compact flux background admits stabilized D7 positions and a small displacement? The paper uses factorized tori, quotient-dependent quantization, and an explicit pair of RR and NSNS three-forms.
How can elementary charge ratios constrain restricted tree-level orientifold flux-potential gradients?
Do physical BPS states satisfy the general convex-hull requirement, how far do boundary bounds extend, and can the pairing formula constrain fourfold flux potentials?
Which internal geometries and scalar stability properties occur in type-II supergravity backgrounds with maximally symmetric four-dimensional spacetime and smeared orientifold/D-brane sources?

How can the large four-dimensional scalar potential induced by U-dual-completed type IIB fluxes be reorganized to expose its flux-bilinear structure, constraints and possible higher-dimensional origins?
How do geometric dualities, enhanced symmetries and a bounded flux D3 charge organize physically distinct SUSY Minkowski F-term solutions on two one-complex-structure toroidal orientifolds?

How do dynamical D6-brane positions, Wilson lines and non-Abelian gauge data modify massive IIA flux compactifications, their four-dimensional scalar potential, AdS vacua and perturbative reliability?
What geometry explains gauge-rank reduction, mixed-sector multiplicities and T-duality in orientifolds with quantized NS-NS B-flux, and what additional consistency conditions arise for K3 orbifolds?

Which fluxes and internal geometries of massive type IIA admit four-dimensional N=1 vacua with SU(3) or SU(2) structure, and how might these backgrounds accommodate chiral D-brane gauge sectors and moduli stabilization?

What are the bulk chiral coordinates, Kähler potential, gauge kinetic functions and flux superpotential of generic type IIA Calabi–Yau orientifolds, and how do their effective actions connect to special G2 compactifications and orientifold mirror symmetry?

How do general fluxes and D6/O6 sources determine the four-dimensional N=1 potential directly from ten-dimensional type IIA, and which consistency conditions and supersymmetric moduli-stabilizing vacua extend beyond truncated N=4 gaugings?
Which moduli can RR, NS and metric fluxes stabilize in a simple IIA orientifold, and can the resulting backgrounds support consistent intersecting-D6 configurations with MSSM-like spectra?

What geometric data determine the four-dimensional N=1 bulk effective actions of type II Calabi-Yau orientifolds, including flux potentials, chiral coordinates, dual linear multiplets and higher-dimensional embeddings?

Construct a T-duality-complete flux superpotential and flux constraints for a simple type II toroidal orientifold, including nongeometric Q- and R-fluxes, and clarify which structures admit local or global geometric interpretations.

Determine the bulk four-dimensional N=1 spectrum, Kähler potentials and flux/torsion superpotentials of generalized type II orientifolds, and test candidate mirrors of Calabi–Yau orientifolds with restricted electric and magnetic NS–NS flux.
How do integral torsion groups determine the consistent BPS D6-brane spectrum, open-string moduli, discrete configurations, and possible chirality constraints in type IIA flux compactifications?

Can intrinsically non-geometric type IIB orientifolds without Kähler moduli stabilize the remaining moduli using quantized R-R and NS-NS fluxes alone, satisfy tadpole cancellation, and yield supersymmetric Minkowski or AdS vacua?
Can non-geometric type II orientifolds admit supersymmetric Minkowski vacua with every retained modulus stabilized, tadpoles satisfied, and parametrically large fields at weak string coupling?

Which ED5, ED1 and closed-string flux effects generate superpotentials in the Type I Z3 orientifold with Wilson lines, how does anomalous U(1) invariance constrain them, and could their combination stabilize moduli?

Can Type IIB orientifolds produce six-dimensional N=1 vacua with multiple tensor multiplets and varied gauge groups, and higher-dimensional examples with useful dual descriptions, especially M-theory on a Klein bottle?

Which toroidal type IIB orientifolds yield consistent D=4, N=1 vacua, how restrictive are their tadpole conditions, and what do alternative projections imply for spectra, candidate heterotic duals and effective interactions?

What type IIB orientifolds are T-dual to elliptic type IIA configurations with O6-planes, especially oppositely charged pairs, and how do twisted tadpole conditions encode four-dimensional N=2 finiteness?
